children: Next week could be an important window to watch for clues as to whether the MATCH Act, which restricts semiconductor equipment and components exports to China, will be enacted soon, Bernstein analysts say in a note. The most prominent restriction under the Act could be of immersion DUV lithography tools from ASML and Nikon, which are essential for all advanced logic and memory chips, they note. "If enacted, it would impede China's ambition to expand capacity and impact all equipment companies' sales to China, not just ASML," they say. The biggest signal watch would be whether the final 2027 annual defense bill, likely released early December, includes the MATCH Act, Bernstein says.(sherry.qin@wsj.com)
